name: Files changed renders the reviewer-ordered diff on seeded data
description: Walks L03b on the seeded PR #482: from the PR list into the detail route, onto the Files changed tab, and over every region of the grouped diff. Like flow 11 this makes NO model call — and here that is the feature rather than a constraint on the test. Smart Diff is deterministic by construction: `GET /pulls/:id/smart-diff` classifies paths with regexes, reads `finding_lines` off the reviews already in the database, and quotes its per-file summary out of the stored patch. `server/test/smart-diff.it.test.ts` proves the recorded-calls half (every provider mock stays empty and the `jobs` table does not grow); what this flow adds is that the whole thing really reaches a browser. Four assertions carry more than their length. 'Core logic' appearing BEFORE 'Boilerplate' is the acceptance criterion — the server returns the groups in that order and the client re-imposes it from its own `GROUP_ORDER`, so a regression in either shows here. The quoted summary 'bucketKey, rateLimit' is the no-LLM claim made visible: those two identifiers were copied out of the `@@` header tails of `src/middleware/ratelimit.ts`'s patch by a pure function, and a model that invented them would say something more fluent. '1 finding' plus 'blocker' is the overlay working end to end across the join that is easiest to get quietly wrong — the seeded review carries `agent_id: null`, so a per-agent reduction keyed on the raw value would collapse it and this badge would simply not exist (see `latestFindingsPerAgent`). And `order=original` in the URL proves the toggle is real state a link can carry, not local component state. DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS FLOW: clicking a findings badge. The badge's click contract — it routes to that finding's card in the Agent-runs tab — is pinned one level down, where it is deterministic: `SmartDiffViewer.test.tsx` proves a badge click reports the file's WORST finding id (and the line-badge and no-badge cases), `FindingsPanel.test.tsx` proves the targeted card is the one expanded ('expands the targeted card, not merely the first one'), and `FindingCard.test.tsx` proves the landing scrolls into view exactly once. The one seam that leaves unpinned is `PrDetailView.openFinding` — the two lines that turn the reported id into `router.push(?tab=findings&finding=…)` — named here so nobody believes it covered. The browser click was removed after FOUR consecutive CI-only failures (runs 31599113842, 31600061139, 31600976140, 31605913685) in which `find role button click --name …` exited 0 while the URL never changed — with the app's navigation demonstrably working: the same steps passed on macOS dev and prod builds, in a linux/amd64 container driving this exact runner against a production build, under a x20 CDP CPU throttle, and on agent-browser 0.33.2 and 0.34.0. Three app/flow-side theories were implemented and disproved in turn (a render-race barrier, kept below because its race is real; `scrollMarginTop` clearing the sticky header, kept in the app because Tab-focus needed it; clicking before the order-flip remount so no stale node can exist — the final run failed with the page scrolled TO the badge and still no navigation). That exhausts every mechanism this side of the locator engine, and the suite already carries a precedent for `find role` misbehaving on CI Linux while `find text` works (flow 10, INSIGHTS 2026-08-07). The full evidence trail lives in e2e/INSIGHTS.md (Open Questions, 2026-08-12); if agent-browser's role engine is fixed or the anomaly is understood, the click steps can come back from this file's git history (9cb8385 has the last full version, probe included). Precondition: a freshly-seeded DB where acme/payments-api PR #482 is the first repo — run via `npm run e2e:hermetic`. NOTE the seed changed in L03b: `SEED_PR_PATCHES` carries real unified-diff text for nine files and the PR row's totals are DERIVED from it, so the summary line reads '9 files · +47'. A database seeded before that has four patch-less rows and this flow will fail on the summary and on every code line. LOCATOR CASING: 'REVIEWER-ORDERED DIFF' is asserted in the RENDERED casing — `SectionLabel` applies `text-transform: uppercase`, so the catalogue's sentence-case 'Reviewer-ordered diff' would time out against a screen that is on and correct. The group labels are NOT uppercased (they are a plain 650-weight span), so those are asserted as written.
